tool_args.old_string: For confounding, a Frisch--Waugh--Lovell decomposition shows the bias is $B(C) = R(C)/D(C)$, where $D(C)>0$ and $|R(C)|$ is bounded by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. The bound ensures $|B(C)| < |\tau|$ whenever the true effect and the omitted-variable bias share the same sign, guaranteeing sign preservation for all column-stochastic $C$. This sign-alignment condition is parameter-dependent but holds generically: it is satisfied whenever the confounder's effect on the treatment and outcome have the same direction, which is the standard assumption motivating adjustment in the first place.
